contract_plain_english: For any real-valued random variable X with mean μ and variance σ², and for every positive threshold t, the probability that X differs from its mean by at least t is at most σ² divided by t².

The conclusion bounds the inclusive two-sided deviation event by the variance divided by the square of the threshold.

definitions_and_conventions: Variance is defined by Var(X) = E(X − E X)^2.
P{|X − μ| ≥ t} denotes the probability of the event on which the absolute centered deviation is at least t.
The source convention lets nonlinear operations bind before expectation.
hypotheses: X has mean μ, so μ = E X.
X has variance σ², so σ² = Var(X) = E(X − E X)^2.
implicit_context: X is defined on an underlying probability space (Ω, Σ, P).
The expectation and variance appearing as the real quantities μ and σ² are well-defined.
No independence, identical-distribution, or special distributional hypothesis is imposed.

details: The result applies to any real-valued random variable having the stated mean and variance.
The threshold is arbitrary subject to strict positivity.
The event is two-sided because it uses |X − μ|.
The threshold comparison is inclusive: |X − μ| ≥ t.
The bound depends only on the variance σ² and not on further distributional information.
The upper bound decays as 1/t² and has numerator σ².

undebatable_constraints: The variable must be centered at its mean μ.
The dispersion quantity in the numerator must be the variance σ².
The result must hold for every t > 0.
The event must be the inclusive event |X − μ| ≥ t.
The right-hand side must be σ²/t².
No independence or distribution-family assumption may be added as part of the mathematical claim.
